findings.F1: Across all hours, a coin's 24-hour return is followed by its opposite over the next day and the next two days, pooled over 6 coins. The slope of the next-24-hour excess return on the standardised 24-hour return has t -11.7 on 16238 non-overlapping cases (t -5.1 on the grid shifted by 12 hours). Over 48 hours the slope's t is -6.8 on 8003 cases (-2.3 on the shifted grid). The lowest fifth of 24-hour returns is followed by +47 bps of unusual move over 24 hours (t 4.4; total +59 bps) and +52 bps over 48 hours (t 2.8; total +75 bps). The highest fifth is followed by -32 bps over 24 hours (t -3.3).
findings.F2: This 24-hour reversal holds coin by coin and year by year. Over 48 hours the slope's t is negative on all 6 coins, from -0.7 (XRP) to -5.2 (XMR). It is negative in 7 of 8 years, at -2.5 or below in 2018, 2021, 2022 and 2023. The exception is 2024, at t +2.0.
findings.F3: The 24-hour reversal comes from the most volatile periods. Split by the coin's past-week hourly volatility, the 48-hour slope's t is -7.7 in the highest third (2669 cases), against +2.1 and +1.8 in the lowest and middle thirds.
findings.F4: Over 5 days the sign turns: a coin's 3-day return is followed by more of the same. The slope of the 5-day excess return on the standardised 3-day return has t 3.0 (3106 cases), and t 3.4 on the grid shifted by 60 hours (3184 cases). The highest fifth of 3-day returns is followed by +72 bps of unusual move (total +129 bps) on the first grid and +185 bps (t 3.7; total +246 bps) on the shifted one. The coin's usual 5-day move is about 1054 bps. Across coins the t is positive on 4 of 6: XRP 2.7, ZEC 2.0, BTC 1.5, ETH 1.2.

findings.F6: The tested evening idea is too small to pay. Its slope's t is 1.70. Its unusual move is +0.10 % per case, 0.5 times the 0.19 % cost of a round trip. The book trails holding the coin on every coin: 2.8 to 5.9 bps a day against 6.7 to 15.5 for holding, and in 6 of 8 years.

ideas.idea: The more a coin has fallen over its last 24 hours, the more it rises over the next day, and the more it has risen, the more it falls; the reversal grows with the coin's hourly volatility over the past week.
ideas.consequence: After a large 24-hour move in a volatile week, a trader leans against it for a day instead of following it, and refuses to chase it.
ideas.name: volatile day move reverses

ideas.idea: The more a coin has risen over its last 3 days, the more it rises over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A strong 3-day rise is a reason to hold a long position for about a week, where the move per case is several times a round trip.
ideas.name: three-day rise continues weekly
